title: Expanding and Factoring Linear Expressions
short: Distribute and factor with negative and fractional coefficients.
trouble: Students distribute a negative to the first term only, writing −(x − 4) = −x − 4.

blocks.html: In Grade 6 you used the distributive property: $3(x + 2) = 3x + 6$. Now the numbers can be negative or fractions, and you will also run it backward to factor.
Expand: multiply the number outside by every term inside: $a(b + c) = ab + ac$. Factor: go the other way and pull out a common factor: $12x - 18 = 6(2x - 3)$. Check a factoring by expanding it again.

A rectangle that is 3 wide and $x + 4$ long can be cut into two pieces, $3 \times x$ and $3 \times 4$. Its area is $3(x + 4)$ and also $3x + 12$. A minus sign in front of parentheses means $-1$ times the group, so $-(x - 4) = (-1)(x) + (-1)(-4) = -x + 4$: every sign inside flips.

blocks.name: areamodel
blocks.cap: $3(x + 4)$ split into $3x$ and $12$. Both pieces are multiplied by 3, not only the first.

blocks.title: Factoring
blocks.q: Factor $12x - 18$ using the greatest common factor.
steps: The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 6.

blocks.html: Distributing to the first term only: $-(x - 4) = -x - 4$. The $-1$ multiplies both terms, so the answer is $-x + 4$. Check with $x = 10$: $-(10 - 4) = -6$, and $-10 + 4 = -6$ ✓, but $-10 - 4 = -14$ ✗.
